text_en: I still have the first drawing someone made of this sky. The ship's windows were too small for it.
Someone keeps leaving street names in the suggestion box. The one with the crooked steps has three now.
I used to count the hours until the next birth. It is a pleasure to wait for other things.
The ship's instruments are steady. I have checked the same numbers twice.
A good work schedule leaves room for the things that go wrong.
I have a spare survey copy. The first copy was accurate. I still prefer two.
I keep finding the same word on tools and doorways. I think it means something you expect to use again.
Your surveyors call it an empty site. Look for steps before you call it empty.
I left my recorder running after the crew went home. The quiet sounded different.
Your map is very bright. The ground outside it is quiet.
There is dust on the edge of the receiver. It looks like frost.
The lamp outside my door has dust on its glass. A little less light reaches the step.
There's a place to come home to on the surface now.
The foundations are complete. Check the Capital District before you expand.
A city needs a name. Look at what was here before you settle on one.
There is another light on the map. Someone will notice it from far away.
The builders have handed over the keys. See what the place gives the City.
Construction complete. The building card shows its current inputs and output.
It's finished. I want to see what people call it once they start using it.
The scaffolding is gone. It makes a different shadow now.
There is something in the archive now that nobody on I-330 knew when we landed.
Research complete. Check the new option before committing resources to it.
Good. Write down how you got there. The result will make more sense with the work beside it.
You found an answer. I wonder what it will sound like when you use it.
The crew has finished. They would like you to see what they found.
Excavation ready. The crew report is waiting at the site.
The digging is done. Bring your questions when you come back.
They reached the bottom. Something down there has waited longer than the crew.
The lander is at the Moon. I used to show you pictures of it from the ship.
The lander has reached lunar orbit. The surface is within survey range.
The receiver can finally listen from up close. Keep the raw recording.
The survey left a marker at the fallen stones. A crew can go down when you are ready.
The Toppled Stones survey is still open. The site is marked on your map.
Bolo kept the raw recording. The crater she marked is still on the survey.
Bolo's signal leads to The Rim Echo. I have left the coordinates on the map.
